 Closings and Delays Dan Carney, Pizza Hut co-founder and Wichita State graduate, dies 
 By Jeffrey Lutz Published : Nov. 16, 2026 at 3:31 PM CST | Updated : 8 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WICHITA, Kan. (KWCH) - Dan Carney, who founded Pizza Hut with his brother, Frank, on Wichita State’s campus in 1958, has died at 95.
 Wichita State University announced the death. Carney graduated from WSU in 1953. He earned his Masters of Business Administration 51 years later.
 Dan and Frank opened the first Pizza Hut in east Wichita, at the corner of Bluff and Kellogg. The business grew into various Kansas locations then became a national chain. 
 It started with a $600 loan from their mother, and the original location was later moved to WSU’s campus.
 WSU said Dan Carney’s legacy extended beyond his business success.
 “For more than seven decades, Dan was deeply committed to Wichita State, sharing his time, leadership and generosity in ways that strengthened the university and created opportunities with countless students,” the university said in a statement on Facebook.
 Carney served as chair and member of both the WSU Foundation Board of Directors and WSU Board of Trustees.
 Carney is survived by his wife, Gayla, and numerous friends and family.
